body:
Camila Reyes: Kicking off customer reference program thread for this push. Goal: 3–5 design partners we can use for reference calls + 2–3 public case studies. Need owners + single source of truth for candidate tracking. Where are we tracking—Drive sheet + HubSpot fields? Want this locked today.

Soojin Lee: For messaging/narrative: I’m owner on story angles + claim language / proof requirements. I’ll also review any outreach copy so we don’t over-promise metrics.

Tyler Benson: Tracking: propose Drive sheet as the working list (fast edits, scoring) + HubSpot as system of record for status + utilization reporting. I can own the sheet hygiene + make sure required properties exist in HubSpot.

Stephanie Nguyen: +1. Sales will live in HubSpot, but the sheet is easiest for the weekly exec readout. Can we define the “stages” so AEs don’t invent their own statuses?

Avery Johnson: Agree. Also: we need a single place to see “OK for calls” vs “OK for public logo/quotes” vs “not yet / NDA only”. Those are different.

Rachel Kim: CS note: we need guardrails on customer load. Before anything goes in “approved for calls,” CSM has to confirm health + escalation history. I can own the CS readiness sign-off step.

Miguel Santos: I can help with outreach coordination + scheduling once we have the shortlist. Also happy to be point person for the customers once they say yes (so they aren’t getting pinged by 5 people).

Isabelle Laurent: For HubSpot, we can add properties: Reference Status (dropdown), Reference Type Allowed (multi-select: call / quote / logo / event), Approval Owner (CSM/Legal), and Last Reference Used Date. I’ll draft the schema + reporting.

Markus Klein: Solutions Eng can validate technical claims + help produce architecture diagrams when we get to drafting. But I’d like a clear “don’t promise” list in the outreach (e.g., exact p95 numbers, GPU types) until we confirm.

Ethan Wallace: I’ll own writing/editing for the public case study assets. For kickoff: I just need confirmed targets + who’s interviewing which customer once we get commitments.

Camila Reyes: Awesome. Decisions:
- Target: 3–5 signed reference agreements, 2–3 published stories.
- Tracking: Drive sheet = working list; HubSpot = source of truth + reporting.
- Owners: Tyler (sheet + ops), Isabelle (HubSpot props + reporting), Rachel (CS readiness), Soojin (messaging + proof), Ethan (writing), Markus (technical validation), Avery/Stephanie (sales asks).

Tyler Benson: Here’s the Drive sheet (working doc): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/REDACTED (tab: “candidate shortlist v1”). I’ll add columns today: readiness score, story angle, “public allowed?” and next action date.

Stephanie Nguyen: Can we set the initial shortlist ask to Sales by EOD? I want each region to nominate top 3 accounts.

Camila Reyes: Yes. I’ll send a note in #sales after this with the ask + link to sheet + deadline.

Avery Johnson: What’s the incentive stance? Customers always ask “what’s in it for us” and I don’t want AEs improvising.

Camila Reyes: Incentives are being finalized (likely options: conference sponsorship credit / extended Optimize trial / charitable donation). For now, outreach should position it as “we’ll make it lightweight + early access / co-marketing support” and we’ll follow up with the exact menu once approved.

Soojin Lee: Please avoid saying “we’ll publish your metrics” in the first email. Better: “We can share outcomes as exact metrics or as ranges, subject to your approval.”

Rachel Kim: +1 and please don’t bypass CSMs. If an AE reaches out cold about references without heads-up, it can backfire.

Tyler Benson: On statuses, propose:
1) Nominated
2) Outreach queued
3) Qualifying call scheduled
4) Verbally committed
5) Legal/consent in progress
6) Approved for reference calls
7) Approved for public case study
8) Published
And a separate “Do Not Contact” checkbox.

Isabelle Laurent: That maps cleanly to HubSpot. I’ll set up Reference Status as a single-select using those exact labels (no custom variants). Also adding “Ref Cooldown Until” date so we can enforce load limits.

Markus Klein: For the “Approved for public case study” gate, we should require: (a) Solutions Eng has validated the architecture diagram + claims, (b) Legal has approved logo/quote language, (c) customer has signed off on final draft.

Ethan Wallace: Works. When we get to interviews, I’ll send a short question bank + what artifacts we need (diagram inputs, before/after metrics source, screenshots optional).

Camila Reyes: Action items:
- Tyler: update sheet columns + share with channel when ready.
- Isabelle: draft HubSpot fields + confirm with RevOps, then post the property list here.
- Rachel: define CS readiness checklist (health criteria + escalation exclusions).
- Soojin: share messaging pillars/approved claim language link.
- Stephanie/Avery: seed the sheet with initial 10–15 candidates by end of week.

Soojin Lee: Messaging pillars doc link (internal): https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/REDACTED — tl;dr: performance economics, reliability/fallbacks, deployment flexibility, operational tooling. I’ll add a “proof needed” column to Tyler’s sheet if that helps.

Tyler Benson: Added a “proof artifacts” column + “metrics publishable? (Y/N/ranges only)” column. Also added owner fields for AE + CSM.

Rachel Kim: CS readiness checklist draft (high level): no open sev-1/2 incidents in last 30 days, NPS neutral+ or explicit champion, no ongoing renewal risk, and customer agrees to a monthly max for calls. I’ll refine.

Isabelle Laurent: HubSpot changes ETA: I can get properties in by tomorrow. Reporting: I’ll set up a simple dashboard: # of approved references, # of requests, utilization last 30 days, and influenced deals (needs tagging, but we can start).

Camila Reyes: Perfect. Keep updates in this thread so we have a single log. Next sync will use the Drive sheet + HubSpot dashboard as the only sources.
